rules.title: California fair housing anti-discrimination and tenant-screening protections
rules.requirement: Housing providers and tenant screening companies may not screen, refuse, or treat applicants or tenants differently because of protected characteristics, including source of income such as Section 8 vouchers. A housing provider may consider criminal history only with limits: it may not use blanket bans, may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile matters, and any conviction-based denial must be directly related to tenancy or safety.

coverage.other_unresolvable: Owner occupancy, shared living area, senior housing, and homeless-youth housing exceptions depend on facts not stated in public assessor data.
coverage.summary: Applies to most California housing accommodations and most housing providers and housing-related service providers, including landlords, property managers, tenant screening companies, real estate agents, homeowners associations, mortgage lenders, and housing authorities.

rules.exemptions: When an owner occupies a home and rents to one additional person, the owner may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics but still cannot make discriminatory statements, notices, or advertisements. When sharing a living area in a single dwelling, the owner or occupant may state or imply that housing is available only to a person of one sex. Qualifying senior housing and, under some circumstances, housing for homeless youth may be limited based on age.
rules.penalty: Remedies listed include recovery of out-of-pocket losses, an injunction, access to housing denied, emotional distress damages, civil penalties or punitive damages, and attorney’s fees.
rules.interaction: The document states that complaints filed with HUD may be automatically filed with CRD, and complaints filed with CRD that allege facts violating the federal Fair Housing Act are automatically filed with HUD.
rules.quoted_span: Screening prospective tenants – including when done by a third-party such as a tenant screening company – in a way that discriminates based on a protected characteristic
